facts_of_case: The plaintiff instituted a Civil suit against the defendants seeking declaration, partition and separate possession in respect of the lands. The parties are governed by Hindu Mitakshara law.

legal_principles.principle: A child born from a void or voidable marriage is entitled to succeed only to the property of his or her parents, but does not acquire equal share in ancestral/coparcenary property.
legal_principles.held: Though Section 16 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 confers legitimacy upon a child born from a void or voidable marriage, such legitimacy is limited in its operation so far as property rights are concerned.
use_in: partition cases involving void or voidable marriages

legal_principles.principle: A child born from a void or voidable marriage is entitled to claim legitimacy and property rights in the property of their parents.
legal_principles.held: Taking into consideration the provisions contained in Section 16 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, the trial Court held that the children born from a void or voidable marriage are entitled to legitimacy and to claim rights in the property of their parents.
use_in: cases involving children born from void or voidable marriages

outcome.final_order: The impugned judgment and decree dated 05.10.2019 passed by the learned District Judge, Bemetara (C.G.) was modified, declaring the plaintiff to be entitled to 1/5th share in the suit property.

use_for_drafting: representing clients in joint family disputes
